article_title: An exploratory study of a new concept macrostructure measure when learning history in middle school
citation: Chen, X., Wang, W., Peng, C., Guo, W., & Clariana, R. B. (2025). An exploratory study of a new concept macrostructure measure when learning history in middle school. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10536-4
title: jRate sorting task software with Pathfinder network analysis for eliciting conceptual macrostructure
description: jRate (Schuelke, 2012) is the computer sorting task software used in both studies: participants drag topic-level key terms around a screen to form clusters according to their understanding, and the software converts the sorting into a proximity file of term-term distances in screen pixels. These files are analyzed by Pathfinder software (Schvaneveldt, 2020) with Minkowski r = infinity and q = n−1 to produce networks compared to an expert referent network by percent overlap and Freeman's graph centrality.
requirements: A computer per participant with jRate installed; an expert referent network of topic-level key terms; Pathfinder software to convert proximity files into networks
constraints: The measure was validated here only for topic-level (macrostructure) terms in history content with explicit chronology, one month after learning
target_learning_goals: eliciting and measuring students' conceptual macrostructure of lesson content
examples: Study 1 used a 43 × 43 proximity array of the Qin terms; Study 2 used a 23 × 23 array of the American Revolution terms
